PARVO CLAIMS POLICE DOGS

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Gross incompetence at a Police K9 Training Facility leads to another parvovirus outbreak – already killing 25 puppies in the last month – this after 76 puppies died last year – same virus, same

Unique Selling Point:
- exclusive footage
- story that broke last year and now we show viewers what happens inside
- insider speaking out against incompetence and cruelty of police management

Summary:
Last year 76 police puppies died of parvovirus. Outrage over incompetence and cruelty at the Roodeplaat K9 Training Facility case the spotlight on the veterinary hospital.

8 months later, nothing has changed. Puppies are dying by the day and while there are the skills to save them, there is a serious shortage of medicine.

We ask who is to blame and who will be held accountable for this cruelty and waste of tax payers money.

Further information:
THE ISSUE
The Canine parvovirus attacks the animal’s intestines, causing vomiting and diarrhoea – it is highly contagious and can easily be prevented by vaccinating puppies and the effective treatment following infection.

The absence of preventative measures (vaccines ad correct hygiene protocols) has contributed to the current situation. Another contributing fact is the delay within the procurement process of necessary medications and vaccines. The veterinary hospital did have the vital medicines necessary for the treatment of any ailments or diseases that may occur.

An April report by the South African Veterinary Council’s (SAVC) facilities inspector Dr Malcolm de Bude sounded the alarm over “critical shortages” of drugs because of procurement issues.

While the report called for all procurement protocols to be addressed within a month, internal police management emails sent in July and August showed nothing was doen to avert eh medicine shortages.

Solidariteit’s Renate Barnard said incompetence and maladministration were to blame. “applications for financial approvals sit on desks for months, Because of recent procurement scandals embroiling senior officers, managers are too scared to sign off procurements.

POLICE STATUS QUO
There is a dire shortage of dogs with over 300 dog handlers without dogs. SAPS allocated R7 million in acquiring dogs since 2016 to address the shortage. The value of a trained dog is approximately R120 000 – the state incurred a potential loss of R9.1 million with the 76 puppies that died in 2019.

Brigadier Vish Naidoo at the time said an investigation was under way to establish if there was any negligence on the part of any member tasked with the safekeeping of the facility and the animals.

The SAVC’s Lynette HAvinga said a follow-up inspection was to be done in Feb – our sources say nothing happened.

Tshwane SPCA chair Jacqui Grove said the outbreak was under control – she could not categorically say the parvovirus had been completely eradicated that Rooodeplaat facility.

FAST FORWARD JUNE 2020
The parvovirus had not been eradicated at Roodeplaat. 25 puppies have died as a result of parvovirus at the K9 training facility – and still counting.

While SAPS claim the dogs have been vaccinated – the cold chain of the vaccinations and therefore the efficacy of it cannot be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. Secondly, there is a shortage of medication to treat puppies that have contracted the virus.

Leading up to our investigation – there was no disinfectant on site, kennels were filthy, but overnight – there was a turn around at the facility when the SPCA showed up for a visit. Our insider thinks the powers that be might have been expecting the SPCA. But even the makeshift disinfection rush didn’t stop the virus claiming puppies – 5 more died that day.

WHAT WE HAVE
Exclusive videos from inside the facility – the dogs are suffering. The kennels are disgusting.

INTERVIEWS
1. INSIDER VET – a young vet doing her community service year has been at the Roodeplaat facility since January – she is horrified at the conditions and is speaking to us – we are hiding her identity.
2. FORMER SAPS VET – we have the option of three vets that have left in the last 6 years who can testify to procurement issues, mismanagement and incompetence.
3. SAPS – confirmed interview
4. SAVC – request in – waiting for response – we have their report and can refer to it if they don’t agree to an interview for Tuesday
5. DOG HANDLER – busy finding someone

COL IVAN MEYER from the Western Cape was set to retire on Tuesday and has been very outspoken – he has not backtracked as he is asking for his disciplinary hearing to be finalised before he retires. Last year he was charged for retiring old police dogs and has been very outspoken criticising the police. If he doesn’t go ahead with interview – I have his statement.

As an alternative we can interview Solidariteit – the police union who has been working on this story very closely and has first hand accounts from dog handlers, vets, procurement officials and give context to the rot at Roodeplaat.

I;ve asked Vish if we can get dog unit access to get footage – fingers crossed.

VO: Police dogs are often the unsung heroes in the fight against crime. Specially bred and expertly trained, they are at the frontlines with their trusted handlers.

But despite the prestige, they are still susceptible to infectious K9 diseases – a hard lesson, the South African Police Service learned in 2019.

LINK: Parvo virus is not new to the Roodeplaat Police Canine facility. Last year more than 70 puppies died of this fast spreading disease. Now there's a new outbreak

VO: This footage was secretly captured in the facility’s veterinary hospital unit just this week. These puppies have contracted the deadly Parvo Virus – most of them are not sleeping. They are dead.

Parvo predominantly affects dogs under a year old - it is a highly contagious, often fatal viral disease characterized by vomiting and severe diarrhea.

VO: The Roodeplaat Police K9 facility breeds, trains and provides medical treatment for police dogs. By October 2019, a lack of vaccines lead to the death of at least 76 puppies infected with parvo virus at this facility.

STRYDOM: But this should not happen in in a facility like like the dog school or the breeding facility.

VO: Retired Police veterinarian Dr Hannes Strydom headed up the facility until 2011. Frustrated Roodeplaat staff and dog handlers still turn to him for advice, sharing their concerns.

STRYDOM: It's a big loss. Each puppy that dies. // is a potential police dog. Which goes down the drain.

LINK: Police dogs are specific breeds and are extremely valuable when fully trained and using the field to detect anything from narcotics to explosives. These are essentially state assets worth tens of thousands of rands

VO: While a 12 week-old puppy is worth roughly R3500 – a fully grown, trained and operational police dog is valued at well over a hundred thousand Rands.

This year alone, over 40 puppies have succumbed to parvovirus at the Roodeplaat K9 Facility, according to our sources.

A figure the police disputes. Brigadier Vish Naidoo is the National Police Spokesperson - he claims it’s far less.

VISH: I think that the measures that we're putting in place to try and contain the spread of this virus amongst the pups it seems to be working.

VO: A statement the insider disputes.

INSIDER: I walked through the cages you literally have to pinpoint that one you must be euthanized. You must be euthanized. It's the worst thing ever// it's not normal. It's the worst

VO: Apparently puppies were vaccinated this year, but despite this, they are still dying by the day with the new outbreak. Even with medical treatment, the survival rate is low.

help but it's not a guarantee that puppies won't get infected.

VO: Renate Barnard represents a police union – its members have been raising alarm around the operations at Roodeplaat since last year.

RENATE: They all actually very stressed because they// all feeling so helpless because we have a duty to do. // But then there's no resources to do it.

VO: Before the outbreak in 2019 – the South African Veterinary Council inspected the facility in April. A report highlighted the problems ranging from critical shortages of medication, the incorrect control of medicine, the incorrect use of the ICU ward for storage and issues around the disposal of animal carcasses.

STRYDOM: These recommendations had certain timelines for compliance // and nobody expected that somebody from the council should have gone back to the facility to inspect.

VO: It was reported that the South African Veterinary Council would do a follow up inspection in February. But it didn’t happen according to our insider.

The council declined an interview – stating the police facility “is registered with this Council as a veterinary hospital” and “meets the minimum standards…. ….in terms of the Veterinary and Para-Veterinary Professions Act”.

The council did not respond to whether a follow-up inspection was done, but stated all facility inspections were being rescheduled.

The insider alleges, not much has changed at Roodeplaat since the Council’s last inspection – carcasses are stacked outside of fridges, the ICU ward is still used for storage and medicine controls are not followed.

RENATE: Two dockets registered, currently under investigation - it’s almost a year later, the dockets have not been sent to the NPA for a decision yet.

Yeah I'm like surprise! you guys HAD it last year it made NEWS. Then we started with this PARVO the outbreak now and it was DOG upon DOG.

PHELE: nothing I can comment on this situation – you’ll get all the comments from SAPS COMMUNICATIONS

VO: While Brigadier Naidoo confirmed the internal investigation into the 2019 deaths was finalized in March – it seems the problems have not all been resolved.

DEREK: Our evidence is that not all the vital medication was available
VISH: we had a shortage // simply because of Of the lack of availability of those at the time that we needed to procure them.
DEREK: But it seems that there's a procurement and supply chain management problem.
VISH: We have to adhere to the Public Finance Management Act. And these things you cannot procure them and keep them for a long period of time.

VO: While there are emergency procurement procedures in place for urgent orders, Barnard feels it’s simply not good enough to leave acquiring medical supplies to the last minute.

RENATE: maybe close down that facility because if they can't take proper care and breed dogs that can be used operationally. What is the use of having that facility.

VO: Tshwane SPCA Inspector Andrew Kekana, has been on the Roodeplaat K9 Facility case since last year. We showed him the footage from inside.

DEREK: is that hygienic
ANDREW: Depending on Which form of hygienic we are referring.
DEREK: Well you told me that it's not great to have the faeces around for example and look at it
ANDREW: It's Difficult to tell How or how long did that vomit and faeces stayed in in in the in the KENNEL
DEREK: // It seems you are giving them the benefit of the doubt. But do they deserve it.
ANDREW: Look no one deserves the benefit if. The suffering of the animals.

VO: Our insider says it’s like this throughout the day.

DERE: Is thre an excuse for that
ANDREW: there’s no excuse cleaning// it must be cleaned up.

VO: We also shared the footage with Brigadier Naidoo – but he declined to watch it.

DEREK: You're not willing to look at any of the videos.
VISH: No, you showing me a video of a place that could have been a video taken anywhere.
DEREK: Well we're telling you it's from Roodeplot me telling you that those conditions are anything but hygienic.
BRIG: // it might be that there is feaces, a dead dog // you and I would never know what the actual context of the pcitures and videos are.

INSIDER: // the truth is the truth is they. It's on paper. It's in the cages. It's in those red bags that the little bodies are lying they must stop denying it.

VO: Brigadier Naidoo promised there would be consequences for any dereliction of duty.

VISH: if somebody is done has done wrong and it can be proven that it was due to the negligence of individuals. Then of course corrective action must be taken.

RENATE: That's the biggest problem in the South African Police Service. They have the rules they have the regulations but it's not been enforced

VO: In the meantime, these puppies are at the mercy of the facility in itscurrent state.

INSIDER: They don't give a shit. It's not just an item. It's not just police property but it's actually a life. You are dealing with.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Gross incompetence at a Police K9 Training Facility leads to another parvovirus outbreak – already killing 25 puppies in the last month – this after 76 puppies died last year – same virus, same
metadata.Unique Selling Point: - exclusive footage - story that broke last year and now we show viewers what happens inside - insider speaking out against incompetence and cruelty of police management
metadata.Summary: Last year 76 police puppies died of parvovirus. Outrage over incompetence and cruelty at the Roodeplaat K9 Training Facility case the spotlight on the veterinary hospital. 8 months later, nothing has changed. Puppies are dying by the day and while there are the skills to save them, there is a serious shortage of medicine. We ask who is to blame and who will be held accountable for this cruelty and waste of tax payers money.
metadata.Further information: THE ISSUE The Canine parvovirus attacks the animal’s intestines, causing vomiting and diarrhoea – it is highly contagious and can easily be prevented by vaccinating puppies and the effective treatment following infection. The absence of preventative measures (vaccines ad correct hygiene protocols) has contributed to the current situation. Another contributing fact is the delay within the procurement process of necessary medications and vaccines. The veterinary hospital did have the vital medicines necessary for the treatment of any ailments or diseases that may occur. An April report by the South African Veterinary Council’s (SAVC) facilities inspector Dr Malcolm de Bude sounded the alarm over “critical shortages” of drugs because of procurement issues. While the report called for all procurement protocols to be addressed within a month, internal police management emails sent in July and August showed nothing was doen to avert eh medicine shortages. Solidariteit’s Renate Barnard said incompetence and maladministration were to blame. “applications for financial approvals sit on desks for months, Because of recent procurement scandals embroiling senior officers, managers are too scared to sign off procurements. POLICE STATUS QUO There is a dire shortage of dogs with over 300 dog handlers without dogs. SAPS allocated R7 million in acquiring dogs since 2016 to address the shortage. The value of a trained dog is approximately R120 000 – the state incurred a potential loss of R9.1 million with the 76 puppies that died in 2019. Brigadier Vish Naidoo at the time said an investigation was under way to establish if there was any negligence on the part of any member tasked with the safekeeping of the facility and the animals. The SAVC’s Lynette HAvinga said a follow-up inspection was to be done in Feb – our sources say nothing happened. Tshwane SPCA chair Jacqui Grove said the outbreak was under control – she could not categorically say the parvovirus had been completely eradicated that Rooodeplaat facility. FAST FORWARD JUNE 2020 The parvovirus had not been eradicated at Roodeplaat. 25 puppies have died as a result of parvovirus at the K9 training facility – and still counting. While SAPS claim the dogs have been vaccinated – the cold chain of the vaccinations and therefore the efficacy of it cannot be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. Secondly, there is a shortage of medication to treat puppies that have contracted the virus. Leading up to our investigation – there was no disinfectant on site, kennels were filthy, but overnight – there was a turn around at the facility when the SPCA showed up for a visit. Our insider thinks the powers that be might have been expecting the SPCA. But even the makeshift disinfection rush didn’t stop the virus claiming puppies – 5 more died that day. WHAT WE HAVE Exclusive videos from inside the facility – the dogs are suffering. The kennels are disgusting. INTERVIEWS 1. INSIDER VET – a young vet doing her community service year has been at the Roodeplaat facility since January – she is horrified at the conditions and is speaking to us – we are hiding her identity. 2. FORMER SAPS VET – we have the option of three vets that have left in the last 6 years who can testify to procurement issues, mismanagement and incompetence. 3. SAPS – confirmed interview 4. SAVC – request in – waiting for response – we have their report and can refer to it if they don’t agree to an interview for Tuesday 5. DOG HANDLER – busy finding someone COL IVAN MEYER from the Western Cape was set to retire on Tuesday and has been very outspoken – he has not backtracked as he is asking for his disciplinary hearing to be finalised before he retires. Last year he was charged for retiring old police dogs and has been very outspoken criticising the police. If he doesn’t go ahead with interview – I have his statement. As an alternative we can interview Solidariteit – the police union who has been working on this story very closely and has first hand accounts from dog handlers, vets, procurement officials and give context to the rot at Roodeplaat. I;ve asked Vish if we can get dog unit access to get footage – fingers crossed.
